type: Environment art redesign, conceptual illustration only
prompt:
Edit Image 1, the existing lakeside game environment concept. Image 2 is the authoritative character identity and rendering-style reference. The user rejects Image 1 because its pretty miniature cottages, flower-covered tourist-village layout, overly neat repeated round shapes and childish small residents do not match the substantial adult ram character in Image 2. Make a major ENVIRONMENT ART REDESIGN, not a color filter or minor decoration pass. Keep the original ram species, the main fisherman's identity and outfit, a highland lake setting, and a social life-game purpose. Change architecture, terrain arrangement, lighting and composition as needed to solve the mismatch. Do not show a character sheet. ONE coherent wide 3:2 gameplay-like environment concept, no text or UI.

PRIMARY GOAL: Make a convincing home and social hub for THIS heavy, powerful, wool-clad mountain species. The landscape, buildings, tools and adult residents must share the character's strong sculptural shapes, charcoal/slate tones, weathered amber, rough woven teal wool, terra-cotta accents and practical craftsmanship. Create curiosity about exploring and an inviting place to join other players. Rugged and expansive, but alive and hospitable.

NEW SPACE:
A sheltered highland lake cove beneath immense worn slate cliffs. The lake is not a decorative tropical pond: cold deep blue-green water, broad rock shelves, a few reeds, rough shore and a practical sheltered fishing landing. Large strong rock masses and wind-beaten grass form the setting. Distant sunlit uplands and a visible narrow trail climbing through a mountain pass invite exploration beyond town. Replace the giant decorative broken arch with credible natural landforms and an old trail disappearing around the mountainside.
The settlement has a clear hierarchy instead of rows of identical little houses. A single substantial communal lodge anchors the midground: low, broad and heavy, rough dark-stone foundation, thick irregular timber supports, broad faceted roof of overlapping weathered slate and close-stretched dark teal wool panels, asymmetric sheltered entrance. Buildings are built INTO the cliff shelves, not arranged as rounded dolls' cottages. A practical open-sided net workshop, fish smokehouse and two partly visible homes cluster around the lodge. Deep eaves and broad timber braces suggest mountain weather. Stone, timber and textile assembly should feel from the same culture as the character's clothing. Use restrained curved structural members, not ram motifs printed on every surface. No oval hobbit doors, grass-roof cottage rows, flower borders, ornate garden pots, fairy village, tent camp, castle, prison, military fortress, giant skulls or totems.
Doorways and circulation accommodate a broad 2.3-meter adult with wide curling horns. Heavy benches, stout work tables, wide uneven low steps, thick rope handrails, large net weights and sturdy wide pier beams all reinforce bodily scale. A few teal and rust cloths echo the character, with broad calm material surfaces. Actual working things: coiled ropes, baskets, worn paths, a drying net, fish smoke from a hearth. Every prop has a reason; don't clutter.

SOCIAL INVITATION AND CAMERA:
Normal third-person gameplay camera a few meters behind the main ram fisherman, approximately his head height with a modest downward angle; broad readable walkable spaces, not a bird's-eye vista or miniature diorama. Keep the main ram in the lower-left foreground, full figure horns to hooves, occupying roughly one-quarter of the image height. Match Image 2: charcoal-blue/cream wool, large curled sandstone horns with one copper repair clasp, teal mantle and cream concentric markings, rust sash, natural cloven hooves, reed basket and bentwood fishing rod. Same adult anatomy and broad heavy proportions.
The main walkable path leads from this character into a sheltered communal shore clearing. Six to nine OTHER ADULT ram-folk in two or three natural groups: fishing shoulder-to-shoulder on a broad low rock landing, warming hands and talking by a modest communal hearth, repairing a net under the workshop overhang. One looks up in greeting; leave a physically visible open seat and standing fishing space. Their bodies must match the reference's substantial adult proportions, not chibi sheep children, mascot villagers or thin human bodies with sheep heads. Players should feel they could walk down this path, choose a spot beside someone, cast a line or enter the lodge.

LIGHT AND STYLE:
Late afternoon after passing mountain weather, clear pale sky opening between clouds. Raking warm sunlight on dark rocks and amber horns, cool blue-green lake and shaded slate cliffs, restrained warm hearth and lodge windows. Strong organized light and shadow with foreground, paths, inhabitants and faces readable. The scene must not be all brown, gloomy, foggy, desaturated or night-time horror. Coherent painterly-textured SCULPTURAL 3D GAME ART matching Image 2, broad exaggerated forms, strong material separation, weathered surfaces with restrained texture frequency. Believable spatial scale. Avoid glossy cinematic realism, storybook softness, sugar-sweet toy aesthetics, busy repeated tiny ornament, overbright resort sunshine and excessive bloom. Preserve the dignity, weight and approachable strength of the character through the whole world.

Maintained ram-folk and teal/rust clothing, while residents show more substantial adult bodies.
Hearth, open lodge entrance and waterside fishing place support visible social activity.
